transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... I guess I've been doing some odd things lately, mostly at church. 

Like, I'll be over by the potluck table, and I'll just stand there holding the serving spoon up in the air, not moving at all. Or... I'll just keep folding the exact same stack of napkins over and over again, even while folks are standing right there waiting on me to move. It's just strange, and I wanted to see what's going on with me.
Have you been feeling unusually sad or hopeless, or perhaps unusually energetic and restless, during the time these episodes have been happening?

No, I wouldn't say that. I haven't been feeling really sad or down in the dumps. And I haven't been bouncing off the walls or anything either. My mood feels pretty normal, to be honest. It's just... those strange things I do at the church that have me bothered.
Have you been hearing any voices or seeing things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. No voices, and I don't see things that aren't there. It's really just... just my body freezing up or doing the same thing over and over with the spoons and the napkins. My mind feels quiet otherwise, no strange sounds or visions at all.
Are you currently taking any prescribed medications, or do you have any known medical conditions that require regular treatment?

No, I'm not taking any medications right now. I don't have any medical problems that I need to see a doctor for, either. I've been pretty healthy, mostly. It's just this new thing with my body acting up at church.
When you are standing there frozen, are you able to hear people speaking to you, and are you able to move if someone gently touches your arm or tells you to stop?

Well, I'm not really sure. When it happens... I don't really remember if I can hear people talking to me or not. And I don't know if I'd move if someone touched me. It's like I'm just stuck there, and I don't really notice what's going on around me until it's over.
Does this freezing behavior happen specifically when you feel stressed, overwhelmed, or reminded of a difficult or traumatic event from your past?

No, I wouldn't say that. It doesn't seem to happen when I'm stressed out or anything like that. It just... happens, mostly at church. I don't really have any bad memories or things from the past that are bothering me, so it's not that. It just comes on out of nowhere, really.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep your thoughts organized or follow along in conversations lately?

Well, I suppose I have noticed something like that. When the ladies at church ask me about things... like the blankets we're making or choir practice... I mean to answer them straight. But then my words just sort of run off. I'll start talking about the green beans I'm canning, and then hymns, and then my roses in the yard. I don't mean to, it just comes out that way. And I can see the folks looking at me, like they can't quite figure out what I'm trying to say to them. It's like my thoughts just don't stay in a straight line anymore.

Outside of these episodes at church, have you noticed that you have less energy, less interest in doing things you used to enjoy, or that you find it difficult to express your emotions or speak with much detail?

No, I can't say that I have. I still have plenty of energy to get my chores done around the house... well, for a woman my age, anyway. I still enjoy tending to my roses and doing my canning just as much as I always did. I feel things the same as I ever have, and I talk just as much, too. It's just... like I mentioned, my words get a bit tangled up sometimes when I'm trying to explain something. But I haven't lost interest in my day-to-day life or felt flat like that, no.
Have you noticed any new physical issues, such as stiffness in your limbs, shaking, or any changes in the way you walk or move around your house?

No, I haven't had any of that. I mean... my arms and legs work just fine. I don't shake at all, and I get around the house the exact same way I always have. I might be a little slower than I used to be, just being my age and all, but... no, no new stiffness or trouble walking.
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of freezing and repeating movements at church?

Well, hold on a second, doctor. I don't freeze up or do any repeating movements at all. Like I was just saying, my body works just fine. But if you mean the... well, the odd behavior, and my talking being so hard for folks to follow... I'd say that's been noticeable for about the past six months. Yes, it's been right around half a year now since that started happening.
Have you ever had these episodes where you get stuck or find yourself doing the same thing over and over again while you were at home or anywhere other than church?

No, doctor. Like I was just saying a minute ago, I don't get stuck or do things over and over. Not at church, not at home, not anywhere. I just don't have that problem at all. It's really just my words getting tangled up like I mentioned.
Do you ever have any strong beliefs that other people find strange or difficult to understand, such as feeling that someone is following you or that you have special abilities?

No, I... I don't have anything like that. I don't think anybody is following me, and I certainly don't have any special abilities or anything. I'm just a regular person. People might have a hard time understanding me when my words get all tangled up, like I said before, but my beliefs are just... well, just normal, everyday things. Nothing strange.
